description.narrative:
Overall objective: African civil society organizations (CSOs) and journalists play a critical role in advancing fair and effective tax and public finance systems at country and regional level and contribute to advancing fairness and financial integrity in global processes.
Impact: African CSOs and Journalists contribute to transparency, knowledge production and dissemination which strengthened public discourse and accountability on fair and effective tax and public finance systems at country and regional level and contributed to advancing fairness and financial integrity in global processes.
Outcome (1) Advanced public discourse and solutions for economic justice and transparency. Indicators: Challenging millions of dollars in tax abuses and Illicit Financial Flows (IFFs). Adopting progressive tax reforms in at least two countries. Increased media coverage to reach over one million Africans. Harmful tax deals deterred. Improve tax compliance. Intermediate outcomes. CSO capacity strengthened. CSOs and tax policy reforms supported. Public engaged. Alliances built. Outputs include International Tax Justice Academy (ITJA), training workshops, policy dialogues, public campaigns, and regional forums, Pan-African Conference (PAC). Indicators. Number of CSOs trained. Number of policy briefs submitted. Numbers of media partnerships formed.
